title: Reliquary identifiers.md DRAFT vectors (kinds 01, 03, 04; text form rd1). Not normative until ADR-0006 is accepted.

content_rules.pattern-mod-251:N: N bytes; byte i is (i mod 251)

constructions.04: inner = HMAC-SHA256(K_root, content); mac = HMAC-SHA256(K, 0x04 || inner)
constructions.key: K = HKDF-SHA256(ikm = S_e, salt = empty, info = ASCII 'reliquary/v1/dedup-id-key/kind=<kk>/epoch=<eeee>/scope=family', L = 32)

text_form: rd1-<kind: 2 lowercase hex>-<epoch: 4 lowercase hex>-<mac: 52 chars RFC 4648 base32 alphabet, lower case, unpadded, last char's 4 unused bits zero>
binary_form: kind (1 byte) || epoch (u16 big-endian) || mac (32 bytes) = 35 bytes

domain_separation_negative.mistake: kind byte 0x01 left out of the MAC input: HMAC(K, SHA-256(content))
family secret S_e used directly as the HMAC key (no HKDF)
HKDF info without the kind/epoch/scope suffix: exactly "reliquary/v1/dedup-id-key"
A1-S3 spike candidate b (info "reliquary/v1/dedup-key/sha256-digest", no kind byte); spike values must never match
digest MACed as 64 hex characters instead of 32 raw bytes
epoch missing from key derivation: epoch-1 ID computed with the epoch-0 key under the same secret
plain SHA-256 used as the ID
kind byte 0x03 left out: HMAC(K, content)
inner MAC keyed with the epoch key instead of K_root
inner value is plain SHA-256 (confuses kind 04 with kind 01)
K_root used directly as the inner key without HKDF (S_root as key)
epoch written little-endian in the binary form

encoding_negative.reason: reserved kind 02 (chunk list) is not a whole-file ID
bare 64-hex string (a plain SHA-256) presented as an ID
